note.p: Given the pattern of visits this looks likely to be a case of Godwin seeking financial or legal advice, and there is an Attorney, Mr Bryant of Callum Street, Fenchurch Street, London, managing bankrupcy cases in these dates. However, many of the calls are after Godwin's bankrupcy, and Godwin also dines with Bryant on a number of occasions. But it is a very one sided relationship - they occasionally 'meet' - probably by chance - but Bryant does not call on Godwin. It is possible that Godwin had struck up an acquaintance with Bryant's of the East India Warehouse on the North side of St Paul' Churchyard. But we have no other evidence of this. In 1828, 1829 and 1832 - there are a number of C Bryant, and one A Bryant. We have coded all these under Bryant as they seem to be connected. And the pattern of Godwin visitng remains stable.
